title: Predictive tenant traffic shaping and soft-quiesce for burst absorption
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a predictive traffic-shaping layer and a non-disruptive soft-quiesce mechanism to Dedicated GPU fleets to absorb short tenant bursts, reduce noisy-neighbor incidents, and preserve contracted throughput guarantees without immediate hard evictions. The feature combines a lightweight burst predictor, ephemeral burst-buffer lanes, grace-token accounting, and coordinated autoscaler inputs so that we can defer hard preemption while staying within latency/throughput SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Burst predictor runs in-serving runtime with <5ms p50 inference added latency on request path
Soft-quiesce reduces hard-eviction incidents by >=60% in staged noisy-neighbor experiments
SLA throughput contracts remain enforced within 5% deviation during 90th percentile burst windows in load tests
Autoscaler receives stable signals from predictor and buffer occupancy and does not oscillate (no more than 2 scale actions in 5 minutes for synthetic spike profiles)
Feature flags allow region-by-region canary rollout and immediate disable with no data loss
implementation_notes: Predictor: simple exponential smoothing + short-window classifier (CPU-affine) running as a sidecar in the serving process; model parameters configurable per-tenant profile
Burst buffer lanes: ephemeral lightweight queues that absorb prefetched KV-cache/sequence prefills and short-lived token bursts; implemented as per-GPU ring buffers with per-tenant accounting
Grace tokens: per-tenant budget that decrement on burst absorption; tokens replenish at contract rate; when tokens exhausted, revert to normal preemption policies
Autoscaler handshake: expose metrics (predicted_burst_score, buffer_fill_pct, projected_10s_rps) to autoscaler; add hysteresis to avoid flapping
Fallbacks: if predictor or buffer unavailable, fall back to current hard-slice rules; ensure synthetic requests never starve production requests via priority bits
Config surface: tenant-level policy with fields: burst_profile (aggressive|moderate|conservative), token_bucket_size, buffer_size_bytes, max_soft_quiesce_duration_ms
Telemetry: emit tenant_burst_events, soft_quiesce_start/stop, token_balance, and preemption_count; hook into Console per-route dashboards
Resource accounting: update billing meter to exclude absorbed ephemeral tokens from billable throughput while within contract-defined grace thresholds
testing_plan: Unit tests for predictor logic and token accounting (CI)
Integration tests: end-to-end in staging with synthetic tenants simulating burst patterns (sudden RPS spikes, long tails)
Chaos test: run noisy-neighbor failure modes while soft-quiesce enabled and verify no tenant SLA violations beyond acceptance thresholds
Load test: run existing perf harness with tenant mix 1000 small-tenants + 50 enterprise-tenants and measure hard-evictions and latency p50/p95
Canary in prod: enable for 2 low-risk customers in us-west-2 for 48 hours, monitor dashboards and oncall alerts
rollout_plan: Feature behind runtime feature flag keyed by tenant and region
Stage 1: deploy predictor + buffer to staging; run full integration suite
Stage 2: limited canary in us-west-2 for 2 customers; run 48h and analyze metrics
Stage 3: ramp to 25% of tenants in us-west-2 and eu-central-1 with close monitoring
Stage 4: global rollout if metrics meet success criteria; otherwise iterate on parameters
Rollback: immediate flag disable will flush buffers gracefully; hard-eviction rules restore within 30s
